status: Registered and pushed before any host run.
question: Does pasting the Shake & Bake brief reduce the host's tool calls, tokens and time before it names the files to change, without lowering how many changed files it names?

cases.source: first 6 of the 12 cases selected in benchmarks/external-recall/frozen-dev20-2026-11-08 (registered hash order); exposed by that run
cases.isolation: each repository copied without .git and without a remote; issue text without URL or number; gold kept outside the case directories
cases.gold: changed_files of the fixing pull request

arms.native: task + issue; host uses its own tools
arms.brief: task + issue + the evidence-only Shake & Bake CLI brief (collector f8041a1, dev20); host may still use its tools
arms.brief_with_drafted_prompt: not run: the local worker (qwen3.5:4b) refused 5 of 6 cases with worker_context_budget, so this arm would equal the brief arm on those cases; recorded as a finding

host.model: sonnet alias, same for every run
host.rules: read only under the case repository; no web, no git network commands, no edits; reading outside the repository invalidates the run
host.answer: last line FILES: [up to five repository-relative paths, most likely first]

metrics.quality: changed files named in FILES (hits at 5) per case; arm totals
metrics.decision_rule: The brief is reported as reducing host work on this sample only if median tool calls AND median tokens are lower in the brief arm AND total hits at 5 are not lower. Otherwise not established. Every run is reported.

limits: one repeat per case and arm; agent behavior varies run to run
public issues may be in the host model's training data, equally in both arms
isolation is by instruction; the host's tool calls are not audited
subagent tokens are host-reported and include cached input; not a bill
